text: Refines D-0337 for #591, step 3 of #564's plan: a prepared Docker Go environment runs a part's Go acceptance with the same Select, Discover, Go producer, collector and repository lifecycle as local checks. It does so through a standard-library transport helper that the prepared image compiles, staged outside the candidate's tree. The helper owns separate stdout, stderr and event pipes and frames them, with process status, over its own Docker connection, without interpreting any test framework. A candidate supplies no authority, and there's no Python, installation, network or host mount. Compiler failures stay setup refusals. All the work shares the existing twelve-minute run and ten-minute phase. Cleanup joins owned processes and removes the container before its staging, and the queue slot is held until cleanup ends. On 2026-11-05 the offline opt-in, which the build's sandbox couldn't run, passed against a prepared pinned Go image on linux/arm64: base failure, production fix, exact child, skip, abrupt exit and forged output.
